title: Core
description: Output, selection, and the universal text rendering used by every other block.

entries.name: PRINT
entries.summary: Write a value to standard output followed by a newline
entries.description: Renders the value with the same rules as TO_TEXT (100-0000005) and writes it to standard output followed by a single line feed.

notes: The line terminator is a single U+000A, never CRLF, on every platform.
Rendering follows TO_TEXT exactly, including 'true'/'false' for booleans.

entries.name: PRINT_LINES
entries.summary: Write each item of a text list on its own line
entries.description: Writes every element of the list to standard output, each followed by a single line feed. An empty list writes nothing.

notes: An empty list produces no output at all, not a blank line.

entries.name: SELECT
entries.summary: Choose between two values based on a condition
entries.description: Returns when_true if the condition holds, otherwise when_false. Both arms are evaluated before the choice is made; this is a selection expression, not a branch.

notes: EAGER: both arms are already-bound values, so both have been computed. There is no short-circuit and no lazy branch in v0.

entries.name: IDENTITY
entries.description: Returns its input. Useful as a key function for SORT_BY and as a placeholder while wiring a program.

entries.name: TO_TEXT
entries.description: Produces the canonical text form of a value. This is the single rendering rule for the whole language; PRINT and PRINT_LINES defer to it.

notes: bool renders as 'true' or 'false' (lowercase) in every backend. Python's native 'True' is explicitly NOT the contract.
int renders in base 10 with a leading '-' for negatives.
list renders as '[a, b, c]' with each element rendered by this same rule.

entries.name: ASSERT
entries.summary: Fail with a message unless a condition holds
entries.description: If the condition is false, execution stops with assertion_failed and the given message. If it holds, nothing happens.

notes: The failure message is written to standard error, not standard output, so it never pollutes a program's comparable output.
